tasks.short: Book rooms, kit and instructors around the shift rosters.

today.trigger: A certificate in Studytube is nearing its end, a class is requested, or a new hire or flex worker has a start date and still needs forklift, VCA or food-safety training.
steps: Collect instructor, room and equipment free time from Outlook and from the site.
Check the AFAS roster so the shift still has enough people, and check CAO rest.
Find a date that also works for an external VCA or forklift exam slot.
Email site managers, revise the date, then enter the session in Studytube and send invites.
Chase no-shows and people who were never on the AFAS roster.
drudgery: Emailing three sites for rooms and names
Rebuilding the grid after one instructor or one peak week changes
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes to finding a slot everyone can live with and to people the first grid missed, especially night shift and agency workers.

lenses.faster: Pulling free time, copying the roster and redrawing the grid disappear. What stays is a short review of the proposed block, plus the exceptions: a peak week, a missing agency certificate, or an exam body that has not confirmed.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job starts when a forklift, VCA or food-safety certificate falls inside 60 days, when AFAS or Recruitee gets a start date, or when an agency order adds a flex worker. It holds seats in Studytube and leaves the week's release to the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Night shift and agency workers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a confirmed seat before the first shift, or before a mandatory certificate lapses, instead of waiting for the next daytime class. Demand would grow if this were cheap, because sites would take small groups every week rather than one quarterly session.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the mail chase and the copy-paste from the roster. The work worth keeping is the conversation with a site manager when a class and a loading peak fall on the same morning.
lenses.options: A mid-week release, a Saturday group, or a smaller group on each shift changes whether a departure is short-staffed or someone works with an expired certificate. The specialist chooses the grid from those options.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from an exception list rather than a blank calendar. They gain the right to fix the order of claims on people's time, mandatory certificate first, then week-one onboarding, then optional courses, and the work becomes more expert in staffing limits and less clerical.
reach: The HR administrator's booking of week-one onboarding sessions, once the specialist learns the AFAS new-hire checklist and document types the administrators use.
The recruiter's check that a Recruitee start date is not fixed while a mandatory certificate is still open. The recruiter keeps the candidate and the offer.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can tell when a slot that meets the written rules is still a bad slot: the shift would be left thin, CAO rest would break, or the external exam body has only been pencilled in. That call keeps an uncertified person off a truck and keeps the day's freight moving.
tasks.pattern_why: Rooms, rosters, expiry dates, staffing minimums and rest rules can be written down and applied in code. A model is the wrong place to decide whether a shift still has enough people.

in_practice.trigger: Each night, and whenever Studytube shows a mandatory certificate inside 60 days, AFAS or Recruitee receives a start date, or an agency order adds a flex worker.
steps: Read AFAS rosters and staffing minimums, Studytube expiry, Outlook rooms and instructors, and agency orders where the feed is structured.
Apply the same rest and maximum-hours checks payroll already uses, and reject any slot that drops a shift below its minimum.
Hold the remaining seats in Studytube and draft Outlook invites, unsent.
Put flex workers with no certificate feed, unconfirmed exam dates and rejected slots on the specialist's list.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist releases each week's block. A slot the rules rejected cannot be put back by the software.
data_needed: Shift roster and the staffing minimum per shift and site
New-hire start dates and agency orders
Rest rules already applied by payroll
in_practice.logs_to: One line per proposal and per release on the SharePoint L&D log, and the enrolment record in Studytube.

evidence.claim: Studytube holds enrolments and certificate expiry, and AFAS holds the roster, so a rules engine can propose seats from data the company already keeps.
Outside bodies certify VCA and forklift skills, so the employer can book preparation and exam slots and cannot issue those certificates itself.
Dutch works-council consent is required for training policy, for personal-data systems and for tools capable of monitoring staff, and a decision without consent can be void within a month.

risks: A class that leaves a night shift below its safe staffing level, or that cuts across CAO rest, is a safety and labour-relations incident.
Flex workers live in the agency portals. A job that reads only AFAS will miss the people who most often arrive without a valid certificate.
The works council can treat automatic reading of rosters and calendars as monitoring under WOR article 27 and withhold consent.
VCA and forklift exam bodies often confirm by phone, so a date in the grid can look booked until the morning of the exam.
research_questions: What share of sessions last quarter were moved after the first proposal, and was the reason staffing, the instructor, the room, the exam body, or a no-show?
Are classrooms, forklift trucks and instructor time already in Outlook or SharePoint as structured calendars?
What share of trainees are flex workers absent from AFAS, and does any of the three agency portals expose their certificates as data rather than a phone call?
Has the works council already consented to using roster data for training plans, or would an automatic booker be a new WOR 27 request?

tasks.short: Build the training spend report that justifies the budget.

today.trigger: The controller asks for the training budget, or month close needs a note on the training accounts.
steps: Export Studytube licences and external course invoices.
Pull training cost centres from AFAS and the three agency bills.
Split mandatory certificates from other courses, by site, in Excel.
Write a short justification and walk it through with the HR Director before it goes to finance.
drudgery: Guessing which site an external trainer invoice belongs to
Rebuilding last month's pivot for a new request
today.time_sinks: The hours go to matching invoices to a site and a certificate, not to the choice of what to fund next year.

lenses.faster: The export, the site split and the pivot disappear once the pack sits on the nightly AFAS extract. About an hour a month remains to check odd lines and to write the note the controller will read.
lenses.autonomous: Month close starts it. The refresh loads coded AFAS, Studytube and agency lines, splits them by site and by mandatory certificate, and holds back any line with no site. The specialist releases the pack.
lenses.ambitious: The controller gets a monthly pack at month close, by site, split into mandatory certificates and everything else, instead of a yearly workbook. Demand would grow if it were cheap: finance would take it at every close, and each site manager would want their own page.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting invoice numbers. The conversation worth having is whether the money kept certificates valid or paid for courses people did not finish.
lenses.options: Fewer external trainers, fewer optional licences, or moving flex-worker induction back to the agencies each leave the sites with a different promise. The three totals side by side are what the HR Director decides on.
lenses.altitude: The workbook rebuild leaves the week. They gain the right to put certificate cost per head, by site, in front of the HR Director before the budget meeting, and the job becomes more expert in the cost drivers.
reach: The FP&A analyst's monthly commentary on the training cost centres, once the specialist learns the chart of accounts and the variance threshold the controller already uses.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can see that a Venlo spike is the seasonal flex intake, between 150 and 300 people, and can defend that sentence to the controller. A total cannot tell that story.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is joins, filters and thresholds on the ledger, invoices and enrolments. Adding up coded lines and flagging a missing site does not need a model.

in_practice.trigger: The payroll month-close date, or a request from the controller.
steps: Refresh training lines from the AFAS general ledger and accounts payable, the Studytube licence and enrolment export, and structured agency charges.
Apply the coding rules for site, mandatory certificate and optional course.
List every line that has no site or no certificate type, and leave it unallocated.
Build site totals and the three scenarios the specialist has defined, with the justification note left blank.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist writes the note and releases the pack to the HR Director and the controller. Uncoded lines are not spread across sites by a rule of thumb.
data_needed: Certificate type on each external course
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history, and the signed monthly pack stored on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI already refreshes HR and finance dashboards from a nightly AFAS extract, so site-level training totals can be a page on data the company stores.
In a 2026 BambooHR survey, desk workers spent 42% of their AI time fixing the output and 35% on the work itself.
Works-council consent covers systems that process employee personal data, which a training-cost report does if it can be opened to a named person.

risks: Agency bills with no site code will be dropped or dumped on Rotterdam, and the pack will blame the wrong place.
A second training total beside the People Analytics dashboard will be ignored, or will start a fight about whose number is right.
Cost per named employee, if it enters the people review, uses personal data the works council has a say in. The flex season, 150 to 300 people, makes a monthly average look like waste.
A generated paragraph about who overspent will be wrong often enough that the controller stops reading the pack.
research_questions: Which AFAS ledger accounts hold training, and what share of last year's training invoices had no site or certificate code?
Do the three agency portals export training fees as data, or only as a monthly PDF?
Which decision in the last budget round would have changed if this pack had existed at each month close?
Can the pack be a page on the People Analytics model, with totals only at site and certificate level?

tasks.short: Design a path from junior roles into site leadership.

today.trigger: The HR Director asks for a successor for a site lead, or a people review shows too few first-line leaders.
steps: See who moved into a team-lead or site role, from which site, and with what preparation.
Talk with the HR business partners and the site managers about what the job requires on a shift.
Draft a path, the time off the floor, and the entry criteria.
The HR Director decides who is invited. The specialist then runs the path and adjusts it after the first group.
drudgery: Restating a generic leadership model in a new deck
Collecting course completions that say little about how someone runs a shift
Chasing written comments from three HR business partners
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in documents and in waiting on managers. The judgment about who is ready happens in one meeting with the HR Director.

lenses.faster: The first pass over CAO job texts, recent internal moves and the old course list shrinks to a draft the specialist corrects. The manager meetings, the nomination and the HR Director's decision take about as long as they do now.
lenses.autonomous: It does not run on a schedule. When the HR Director opens a round, a draft of two or three path designs is prepared from job texts and past moves, and it stops with the specialist. Nothing goes to a manager or into a personnel file until the specialist has rewritten it.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse shift leads in Tilburg and Venlo, as well as office staff in Rotterdam, get a first-line path toward team lead and site lead. Demand would grow if the design work were cheaper, because each site manager would ask for a group, and the HR Director would still cap the seats.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss another generic leadership deck. The time they want is with a shift lead and a site manager, checking that the path matches a late truck and a short crew.
lenses.options: A rotation across two sites, a mentor who is a sitting site manager, or a short Studytube path plus a real assignment make different people ready and put different load on the floor. The HR Director's choice of design changes who can enter.
lenses.altitude: Less of the week goes to curriculum documents. They gain the right to propose the entry criteria and the shape of the path; the HR Director keeps the invitation. The job becomes more expert in first-line work on the three sites.
reach: The HR business partner's preparation notes for the talent conversation on warehouse team leads, once the specialist learns that review and the CAO job levels the partners use. The partner keeps the site relationship.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist, with the site manager, can judge whether someone can hold a shift when a truck is late and two people are absent. Course completions cannot show that, and a score from learning data would be the wrong input to a promotion.
tasks.pattern_why: The path depends on the site, the person and what the HR Director will sponsor, so the steps are not a fixed workflow. The specialist stays the lead; help is limited to drafts and comparisons.

in_practice.trigger: The HR Director opens a succession or first-line leadership round.
steps: Gather CAO job texts, recent internal moves from AFAS and the current Studytube leadership catalogue.
Draft two or three paths, each with time off the floor, a mentor and what 'ready' means in observable work.
The specialist rewrites the drafts with the HR business partners.
The HR Director chooses the design and names the people invited.
Any exercise that uses a model is labelled as AI, and completion of it is not written into the appraisal.
in_practice.human_gate: No invitation, no note on the personnel file and no enrolment until the HR Director decides. The specialist does not pass that decision on.
data_needed: CAO job profiles for team lead and site roles
Current courses and time they take
in_practice.logs_to: The program file on SharePoint, including the HR Director's decision. Not the AFAS appraisal.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's learning agent shows skill gaps, pathways and mentors, and HR still guides role moves and leadership development. The write-up gives no outcome figures.
In a randomised trial of 52 junior developers, those who used AI scored 17% lower on a later mastery quiz; those who asked for explanations retained more.
From 2 December 2027, AI that uses learning data to evaluate workers falls under Annex III point 4(b) as high-risk.
Training policy requires works-council consent under WOR article 27(1)(f).

risks: A ranked potential list drawn from Studytube evaluates workers. From 2 December 2027 that is high-risk, and the works council already has a consent right on training policy and personal data.
A path written for Rotterdam office staff will not prepare a Venlo shift lead, and the site managers will ignore it.
If people let an assistant do the exercises, they can finish the path and still be weak on the floor. The developer trial showed lower mastery when the assistant did the work.
Nominations that skip the HR Director, or that the works council reads as a hidden assessment, will stop the program.
research_questions: Of the people who became team lead or site lead in the last three years, how many came from the warehouse, from which site, and what preparation did they actually get?
Will the HR Director keep the invitation decision, and accept entry criteria that are not a score?
Can a shift lead be released for a rotation without breaking the roster, and will Tilburg and Venlo managers sponsor that release?
Would the works council treat a pathway tool that profiles employees as a WOR 27 matter on training policy and personal data?

tasks.short: Build site training on fuel, waste and energy use.

today.trigger: QHSE or a site manager asks for a session after a fuel, waste or customer question, or the yearly toolbox talk comes round.
steps: Collect the site instruction and last year's slides from SharePoint.
Agree with QHSE which behaviour should change.
Write a toolbox talk or a short Studytube module, usually in PowerPoint.
Run it for people who are on day shift, and file the attendance.
drudgery: Turning a procedure PDF into slides
Changing the date on last year's deck
Collecting attendance from a daytime session
today.time_sinks: The few hours go into the deck and into a daytime talk that night shift and flex workers do not attend.

lenses.faster: The blank-page outline, script and questions disappear, because Studytube can draft them from the approved instruction. Choosing the behaviour, checking the draft against the yard and the QHSE sign-off remain, and they are most of the time that is left.
lenses.autonomous: A new or replaced fuel, waste or energy instruction on SharePoint starts one drafting call into Studytube. The draft is not published, and nobody is enrolled, until the specialist and QHSE have signed.
lenses.ambitious: Night shift and agency workers, who miss the daytime toolbox talk, get a short module in their first week, written from that site's instruction. Demand would grow if drafting were cheap, because Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo would each want their own version.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the slide deck. The hour they want is on the floor, with a driver or a picker, to see whether idling, waste sorting or energy use is a skill problem at all.
lenses.options: A poster and a team brief, a Studytube module, or a yard walk with the supervisor change different things: a completion tick, or a driver who shuts the engine off. The drafts make that choice before anyone is enrolled.
lenses.altitude: Those hours move from slides to a sign-off with QHSE and a check that night shift and flex workers are in scope. They gain the right to send a request back when a course is the wrong tool, and the job becomes more expert in that choice.
reach: The training half of an HR business partner's briefing when a site changes a working method, once the specialist learns that site's work instructions. The operations manager still owns the method.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist can spot a drafted step that reads cleanly and would be unsafe, or simply ignored, on a night shift. QHSE signs the working method. The model does not.
tasks.pattern_why: With a signed instruction as the only source, one model call can produce an outline, a script and questions that a person checks. The work does not need an agent that finds its own steps.

in_practice.trigger: QHSE uploads or replaces a fuel, waste or energy instruction on SharePoint.
steps: Send that document to Studytube AI Authoring as the only source.
Receive a Dutch outline, script and questions, marked as a draft.
The specialist checks site facts, names and any sentence that tells someone how to work.
QHSE signs the draft or returns it.
Publish only to the agreed groups, including night shift and flex workers where the roster allows.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist stops a draft that goes beyond the instruction. QHSE signs before anyone is enrolled. There is no automatic publish.
data_needed: The current signed instruction for that site
Who must take it, by shift and including flex workers
The Dutch terms the site actually uses
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube version history and the signed copy on SharePoint, with the reviewer's name and the date.

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring, the LMS Noordhaven already uses, drafts outlines, scripts and questions from an uploaded PDF, PowerPoint or SCORM, and the author edits them.

MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, a person reviews, and they describe the tool as support rather than the decision. The account gives no measured learning result.
Workday's own account of its learning workflow advises setting a baseline before launch.
An AI system that interacts with people must disclose that it is AI, and inferring emotions at work is prohibited.

risks: A fluent module can contradict the site work instruction or VCA practice. Published without the QHSE sign-off, it trains people on the wrong method.
Completions can rise while fuel use and waste do not move. The sources do not show a course cutting time-to-skill.
Night shift and flex workers can be marked complete on a phone without having practised the task.
A tutor added on top of the module must say it is AI, and it must not infer emotion from a camera or a voice. A change to training policy still needs works-council consent.
research_questions: Is the fuel, waste and energy instruction for each site written down and current, or does it live with the supervisor?
Who may sign a training text that restates a working method, and is that person in QHSE?
What share of the last toolbox talk's audience was night shift or agency staff?
Which figure, idling hours, waste tickets or energy per pallet, would have to move, and is a course a lever on it at all?

role.altitude: The two specialists become the people who keep the competence record honest for about 1,200 employees and the flex pool: who may start a shift, which forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates lapse, and the Article 4 file that shows what Noordhaven has done on AI literacy since 27 July 2026. The HR Director still decides who moves into a leadership role.
reach: HR administrator: chasing missing certificates and booking week-one onboarding, after they learn the AFAS checklist.
Recruiter: the check that a start date is not confirmed while a mandatory certificate is missing. The recruiter keeps the offer.
FP&A analyst: the monthly note on the training cost centres, after they learn the controller's variance rules.

HR business partner: the training half of a changed working-method briefing, and the preparation notes for a first-line conversation with warehouse team leads. The partner keeps the site relationship.
role.ceiling_note: Two people, at a loaded EUR 68 an hour, cannot take the three HR business partners' site relationships or the payroll close. External bodies issue VCA and forklift certificates, and practice on the truck stays with a qualified instructor. Works-council consent bounds new tools that use personal data or can monitor staff, and from 2 December 2027 learning data used to evaluate workers carries the high-risk duties. Shift staffing limits how many people can leave the floor. Drafts can multiply; sign-off and floor practice cannot.
skills_to_grow: AFAS roster and certificate fields, and the training ledger, well enough to set rules a booker and a cost pack can run.
The controller's cost-centre logic and the invoice formats of the three staffing agencies.
How to keep an Article 4 measures file, and how to take a WOR 27 request to the works council with the HR Director.
First-line work on a warehouse shift, so a leadership path describes the job.
Reading a QHSE work instruction closely enough to reject a drafted step.
role.ambitious_version: Every new hire and every flex worker is certified before the first shift, on day and night shift, at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and the week-one onboarding record matches what happened. Warehouse leads at Tilburg and Venlo have a path toward team lead that the HR Director sponsors. The specialists can show the works council one file on what the company has done for AI literacy under Article 4. The figures they report are first-shift certification, week-one onboarding and who is still productive at day 90.
